headline: New law directs the Commerce Department's tourism office to promote travel to U.S. music attractions and international travel to U.S. sports events.
what_it_does: The law tells the National Travel and Tourism Office, part of the Department of Commerce, to promote travel within the U.S. and from abroad to American music festivals, concert venues, and other music-related places. It also widens the office's existing sports and recreation work to include promoting international travel to sports events in the U.S. The office must report to Congress on its work within one year, and then every two years after that.

who_it_affects.group: Music festivals, concert venues, and other music-related attractions
who_it_affects.how: They may be included in federal efforts to attract visitors from the U.S. and other countries.

who_it_affects.group: Organizers of sports and recreation events in the U.S.
who_it_affects.how: Their events may be promoted by the federal tourism office to travelers from other countries.
The office takes on new promotion duties and must send regular reports to Congress.
It will receive a report within one year and then every two years on the office's activities and findings.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 9, 2026; the first report to Congress is due within one year after that, then every two years.
